# temps_api_key (Resource)

A Temps API key, for CI, scripts or another Terraform workspace.

Temps returns the key only when it is created, so it is kept in state as a sensitive value: protect the state file. An imported key has no `key` value; replace it to mint a new one.

A key can never grant more than the key that creates it: Temps refuses a role or permission the provider's own key lacks. Temps cannot change a key's role, permissions or scope, so changing them replaces the key.

Import with the key ID.

Required API key permissions: `api_keys:read`, `api_keys:create`, `api_keys:write`, `api_keys:delete`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "temps_project" "web" {
  name = "web"
}

# A key for a CI job that only reads deployments of one project.
resource "temps_api_key" "ci" {
  name        = "ci-read-only"
  role        = "custom"
  permissions = ["projects:read", "deployments:read"]
  project_id  = temps_project.web.id
  expires_at  = "2027-06-30T00:00:00Z"
}

output "ci_key" {
  value     = temps_api_key.ci.key
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name, unique on the server.
- `role` (String) Role: one of `admin`, `platform_admin`, `user`, `reader`, `api_reader`, `custom`. `custom` takes `permissions`.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) `false` deactivates the key without deleting it. Defaults to `true`.
- `environment_id` (Number) Restrict the key to one environment of `project_id`.
- `expires_at` (String) RFC 3339 time after which the key stops working. Must be in the future. Unset, Temps expires the key one year after it is created.
- `permissions` (Set of String) For `role = "custom"` only: the permissions the key has, for example `projects:read`. Changing them replaces the key.
- `project_id` (Number) Restrict the key to one project.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Numeric key ID.
- `key` (String, Sensitive) The key, known only to the run that created it.
- `key_prefix` (String) First characters of the key, to recognise it in logs.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The key value is shown only when the key is created, so an imported key has
# no `key` attribute.
terraform import temps_api_key.ci 42
```
